sources.title: History of Gucci
sources.locator: 1921 origin, company heritage; live branded retrospective
sources.limitations: Company statement: first boutique opened in Florence in 1921. Retrospective, not neutral forensic history.

sources.title: 2003 Form 20-F, history and ownership
sources.locator: Item 4.A Significant Historical Events, lines 691-723; Item 4 settlement, lines 1648-1667
sources.limitations: Primary company chronology: 1987–89 half sold, 1993 remaining half, IPO 1995, second sale 1996, revenue 1998, LVMH/PPR 1999. Filing dates founder 1923, contrary to company's current 1921 history.

sources.title: Paolo Gucci v. Gucci Shops, Inc., 688 F.Supp. 916 (1988)
sources.locator: Decision Background and court findings, especially lines 77-109
sources.limitations: Court record covers family branches, Rodolfo's 1983 death, 50% ownership at case time and Paolo's right to describe design work but not use Gucci as brand.

sources.title: Family Feuds: Gucci's Empire Splits a Seam (June 20, 1988)
sources.locator: Article opening, announcement of 47.8% stake sale
sources.limitations: Contemporary estimate/initial announcement, stake size may differ from later completed 50% over 1987-89.

sources.title: Bahrain Bank Buys Out Gucci, Puts an End to Legal Wrangle (Sept. 28, 1993)
sources.limitations: Contemporaneous completion report; sale estimated $150m–$200m in published reports, not audited consideration; records claims of mismanagement and dispute.

sources.title: The Gucci wife and the hitman (July 24, 2016)
sources.locator: Family recollections, brand licensing discussion and 1995 murder
sources.limitations: Retrospective, includes interviewee claims and potentially subjective assessments; corroboration needed before precise causal attribution.

sources.title: Gucci house information and timeline
sources.locator: History; 1921 foundation; 1994 Tom Ford; 1999 Gucci joins group
sources.limitations: Current owner-branded account supports 1921 and the later corporate affiliation; ownership terms better supported by SEC.

sources.title: 2004 Schedule 14D-9, 2004 PPR offer
sources.locator: 2004 offer introduction; PPR 66.83% voting power; transaction chronology
sources.limitations: Primary filing for later PPR voting stake, not evidence of 1993 family sale.

sources.title: The battle for Gucci turns personal (March 9, 2001)
sources.limitations: Contemporary interpretation. Business contest occurs after the family had exited.

sources.locator: June 10, 1988 report: 4 of 8 seats, fifth seat proposal, custodians of disputed 50% block
sources.limitations: Contemporary reporter citing sources, not official recorded board minutes.
